title: Delhi High Court Restrains 'Benne Delhi' From Using the BENNE Mark Against Bengaluru Dosa Chain
case_name: Shimow Hospitality Private Limited v. Benne Delhi & Ors.
card_summary: Justice Vikas Mahajan granted an ex parte ad interim injunction to Shimow Hospitality, which runs the Benne dosa chain modelled on Bengaluru's Darshini culture, against a Delhi outfit trading as Benne Delhi. The court found a prima facie case of passing off and a risk of irreparable injury, restraining the defendant from using BENNE, BENNE DELHI or any deceptively similar mark until the next hearing.
card_tip: Register and police a coined or regional-language brand name early; a restaurant chain built around such a mark can get ex parte relief against a close imitator before the defendant is even heard.
verification_notes: Bar and Bench, LiveLawBiz and Medianama agree on the bench (Justice Vikas Mahajan), the case number CS(COMM) 1131/2026, the 16 October 2026 date, the parties, and the scope of the restraint. SpicyIP and LawChakra corroborate the prima facie and balance-of-convenience findings. This is an interim, ex parte order; the defendant has not yet been heard, and further hearings are listed before the Joint Registrar and the Court.
